build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player stocks shelves by dragging items onto display positions and sets prices via a slider or input. Adventurer customers browse, evaluate prices against their visible budget, and buy or leave. Score 0 if no pricing mechanic exists.

Customers have visible budget indicators and item preferences. Overpriced items are rejected (customer scoffs and leaves). Underpriced items sell quickly but reduce profit. The pricing sweet spot is the core decision. Score 0 if customer behavior is random regardless of price.

Thieves occasionally grab items and run for the door. The player must click to chase or activate pre-placed traps to stop them. Failed theft prevention loses inventory. Score 0 if no theft mechanic exists.

A dungeon phase lets the player enter a procedural side-scrolling dungeon with simple combat to collect loot for restocking the shop. Better dungeon performance yields better inventory. Score 0 if no dungeon phase exists.

The run ends in victory (reaching a gold target) or bankruptcy (running out of stock and gold). Both outcomes have distinct result screens. Gold persists between shop and dungeon phases. Score 0 if no win/loss condition exists.

At least 8 distinct item types exist (swords, shields, potions, armor, rings, scrolls, etc.) with different base values and customer appeal. Items have visible quality tiers. Score 0 if fewer than 4 item types exist.

At least 4 distinct customer types with different budgets, preferences, and behaviors (bargain hunters, collectors, warriors, mages). Customer mix changes over days. Score 0 if all customers are identical.

Shop upgrades are purchasable between days: display cases (hold more items), security (traps, alarms), larger floor space, and decorations that attract better customers. At least 4 upgrade types. Score 0 if no upgrades exist.

The dungeon phase has procedural generation with at least 3 enemy types and collectible loot of varying quality. Dungeon difficulty increases on later days. Score 0 if the dungeon is static or has no enemies.
A results screen shows days survived, total profit, thieves caught, best single sale, and dungeon floors cleared. Score 0 if no results exist.
A styled title screen shows a cozy shop interior with items on display. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The game flow connects title -> shop day -> dungeon phase -> upgrade screen -> next day without restarting. Score 0 if transitions are missing.
During the shop phase, gold balance, item prices, customer budgets, and inventory are clearly visible. During dungeon, health and loot collected are shown. Score 0 if no displays exist.
Readability at 1280x720 is strong: items, customers, prices, shelves, and the shop layout are all clearly distinguishable. Score 0 if elements blend together.

The art direction is coherent across title, shop, dungeon, customers, items, and UI — a consistent fantasy shopkeeper aesthetic with warm palette. Score 0 if mostly default UI or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
Items have distinct illustrated sprites, customers have character art, and the shop interior uses real tile/sprite assets — not plain ColorRect fills. Score 0 if items or customers are text labels.

HUD and UI chrome: price sliders, gold display, customer panels, upgrade shop, and result screens use styled themed widgets — not raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled.

Animation and feedback: customers browse with walking animations, purchases produce coin effects, thieves run with urgency, traps trigger with visual flair, and the dungeon has combat animations. Score 0 if all state changes snap silently.
